sources.description: Financial events from Amazon Finances. date is the marketplace-local date of the winning transaction posted time (America/Los_Angeles for US and CA). Once released it matches Transaction Release Date; while still deferred it is the local date of the deferred posting, and it can be one day earlier than the UTC posted timestamp near midnight. transaction_posted_date matches the Amazon Transaction report date/time column and is earlier than date for deferred orders. transaction_release_date matches Transaction Release Date and equals date once released. shipping_promotion_rebate is the order shipping promotion, a rebate to the customer and not an Amazon fee; promotion_fee holds the same values and is kept for backward compatibility. settlement_type REFUND is a money event, not a warehouse return. ORDER rows use order-date COGS; REFUND rows use return-receipt-date COGS (0 when no return). COGS is stored negative. All columns other than "total" express a single type of cost/fee/income. Expenses are negative values (standardize this when comparing with other tables). total_non_principal_amount is total minus item_price in the payout sign. total_fees holds the same value and will be removed on 2026-10-31. marketplace_facilitator_vat / refund_marketplace_facilitator_vat are MarketplaceFacilitatorVAT-* ItemWithheldTax lines (EU/UK); US MarketplaceFacilitatorTax-* stays in item_withheld_tax / refund_item_withheld_tax. fba_inbound_transportation_fee and fba_inbound_transportation_program_fee are the base fee amounts from Amazon Finances. When Amazon reports tax on those fees separately, that tax is in item_tax. DataDoe does not estimate this tax by dividing the fee. Settlement report base fee amounts stay on the fee column, and settlement report tax on fee lines map to item_tax. There is no dedicated Lightning Deal Fee column because Finances does not distinguish Lightning from Best Deal; those amounts are in deal_participation_fee. Refund Customer Return - Not Received is not available from Finances. Merchant-fulfilled Buy Shipping label fees (LabmanLabelPurchase / LabmanLabelReturn / LabmanLabelChargeBack) attach to the order SKU when that order has a single SKU in the Amazon order report. Amazon settlement start, settlement end, and deposit timestamps are not columns on this table. They are on the raw finances transactions table when a settlement report header matches the settlement ID. The deposit timestamp is the time Amazon starts the funds transfer, not the time the money arrives at the bank.

dataAvailability.description: The daily fetch starts at 2am and rereads 8 days. Fetches also start at 10am and 4pm, including weekends, and reread 2 days, including the current day. US and Canada use Pacific time (America/Los_Angeles) for the 10am and 4pm fetches, including daylight saving. Other marketplaces use their local time zone. Amazon may leave out orders from the last 48 hours. These times are when the fetch starts. Rows appear after Amazon publishes them and after DataDoe finishes processing and export.

issues.title: SQP data is available only for selected ASINs
issues.description: DataDoe downloads SQP data only for ASINs you configure. Open your Sellers & Vendors list in the app, select a Seller in a supported marketplace, then choose SQP ASINs to add up to 252 ASINs per connection. SQP is not available for Vendor accounts or some Amazon stores. If the list is empty, no SQP data is downloaded for that Seller.

issues.title: SQP is available only for Seller Central in supported Amazon stores
issues.description: Amazon Search Query Performance reports are available only for Seller Central accounts in North America (all stores), Far East (all stores), and these European stores: Spain, United Kingdom, France, Netherlands, Germany, Italy, Sweden, Turkey, Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates, and India. Vendor accounts and other stores cannot download SQP data.

sources.description: Successful Amazon Catalog Items observations per child ASIN and marketplace for items the Organization tracks. A later successful response is retained even when unchanged; a retry keeps the original observation_id and checked_at without adding a duplicate. History starts after the Organization enables it and tracks the item. A newly associated item receives its next successful observation, without older shared-cache history. The source stays off until a staged Connector rollout enables it. History follows the existing catalog refresh. DataDoe can request an item again one day after its last cache update. The catalog worker runs every 15 minutes in each region and stops at its time limit, so a tracked item can go more than one day without a new observation. A history delivery backlog does not stop current catalog refreshes. Failed, throttled, empty and hard-failed attempts and items Amazon omits create no history observation. Missing days and source values remain unknown: a missing item or rank does not mean deletion or a zero rank. Observations are per item, not an atomic snapshot of the whole catalog. Changes occurred between observations; checked_at is not the exact time Amazon edited the item. Use amazon_products_by_child_asin and amazon_products_raw for current-state joins to sales, inventory and profit. They keep one latest row per ASIN and marketplace and provide the cached onboarding baseline. Legacy rows can have null checked_at and observation_id; overwritten payloads are not recovered or assigned invented times. When Amazon omits an item, its current row is created or cleared without a new checked_at and without a history observation. Filter history by child_asin, marketplace_id and a date range; date and snapshot_date are the UTC date of checked_at. For rank trends, order by checked_at and observation_id and compare category names and raw category identifiers, which can change. To compare observations, join on child_asin and marketplace_id and filter the two observation_id values; an absent observation produces no comparison. For the last observed state at a chosen time, filter checked_at <= the chosen timestamp, then use QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY child_asin, marketplace_id ORDER BY checked_at DESC, observation_id DESC) = 1. This returns only items observed by that time and does not fill gaps with current content.

columns.description: Amazon Seller Central seller ID from the connection (connection_seller_id). Null when the connection has no seller ID.

columns.description: Vendor coupon campaign id. Empty string on seller coupons, which have no campaign.

columns.name: campaign_name
columns.description: Vendor coupon campaign name. Empty on seller coupons.

columns.name: vendor_code
columns.description: Amazon vendor code on the coupon campaign. Empty on seller coupons.

columns.name: is_subscribe_and_save
columns.description: Whether the vendor campaign is a Subscribe and Save offer. Empty on seller coupons.

columns.name: budget_type
columns.description: Vendor campaign budget allocation: PER_INDIVIDUAL_COUPON or SHARED_BUDGET. Empty on seller coupons.

columns.name: campaign_total_clips
columns.description: Sum of clips across coupons in the vendor campaign. Campaign-level value repeated on every coupon and ASIN row. Aggregate by campaign_id before summing.

columns.name: campaign_total_redemptions
columns.description: Sum of redemptions across coupons in the vendor campaign. Campaign-level value repeated on every coupon and ASIN row. Aggregate by campaign_id before summing.

columns.name: currency_code
columns.description: ISO 4217 currency of the coupon amounts.

columns.name: website_message
columns.description: Message displayed with the coupon on the product page.

columns.name: start_date_time
columns.description: Coupon start in UTC. Use this column for date filtering; the table has no date column.

columns.name: end_date_time
columns.description: Coupon end in UTC.

columns.name: is_once_per_customer
columns.description: Whether a vendor coupon can be redeemed once per customer account. Empty on seller coupons.

columns.name: customer_segment
columns.description: Customers who can clip the coupon. Examples: All (Default), Amazon Prime, Amazon Student.

columns.name: clips
columns.description: Times customers applied the coupon on the product page. Coupon-level value repeated on every ASIN row of the coupon. Aggregate by coupon_id before summing.

columns.name: redemptions
columns.description: Times the coupon was used for a purchase, including returned and cancelled orders. Coupon-level value repeated on every ASIN row of the coupon. Aggregate by coupon_id before summing.

columns.name: budget
columns.description: Budget allocated to the coupon for discounts and clip or redemption fees. Present for seller coupons and for vendor campaigns with PER_INDIVIDUAL_COUPON. Empty when the vendor campaign uses SHARED_BUDGET.

columns.name: total_discount
columns.description: Amount customers saved with the coupon, including returned and cancelled orders. Coupon-level value repeated on every ASIN row of the coupon. Aggregate by coupon_id before summing.

columns.name: budget_spent
columns.description: Amount spent on the coupon, including clip fees and redemption fees, and including returned and cancelled orders. Coupon-level value repeated on every ASIN row of the coupon. Aggregate by coupon_id before summing.

columns.name: budget_remaining
columns.description: budget minus budget_spent. Empty when the vendor campaign uses SHARED_BUDGET.

columns.name: budget_percentage_used
columns.description: Percent of allocated budget spent, on a 0-100 scale. A value of 0.4 means 0.4 percent. For a shared vendor budget this is versus the campaign budget.

columns.name: sales
columns.description: Seller coupon revenue after the discount, including returned and cancelled orders. Empty on vendor coupons. Coupon-level value repeated on every ASIN row of the coupon. Aggregate by coupon_id before summing.

columns.name: merchant_id
columns.description: Seller merchant customer id. Empty on vendor coupons.

columns.name: promotions_api_mapping_id
columns.description: Identifier for joining this coupon to amazon_promotions.

columns.name: asin
columns.description: Child ASIN included in the coupon. One row per ASIN.

columns.name: discount_type
columns.description: PERCENT_OFF_LIST_PRICE or AMOUNT_OFF_LIST_PRICE for this ASIN.

columns.name: discount_amount
columns.description: Customer discount on this ASIN. A percent of list price when discount_type is PERCENT_OFF_LIST_PRICE (10 means 10 percent). A currency amount when discount_type is AMOUNT_OFF_LIST_PRICE.

sources.description: Seller and vendor coupon performance, one row per coupon and ASIN. Includes clips, redemptions, budget, and the ASIN discount. Campaign and coupon totals repeat on every ASIN row. Vendor rows carry campaign, vendor code, and Subscribe and Save; sales is seller coupon revenue. Filter on start_date_time. Join amazon_promotions on promotions_api_mapping_id.

sources.description: Lookup of DataDoe Amazon accounts for Seller Central, Vendor Central, Amazon Ads, and Amazon DSP. sources.description: Your uploaded product cost ledger, maintained by the user. Seller costs are per SKU and ASIN; vendor costs are per account, marketplace, ASIN and effective date with empty SKU. Vendor rows can have optional vendor-code, fulfillment and exact-PO variant keys; an empty set of variant keys is the explicit ASIN default. The full variant key and effective date identify an upsert or edit. Uploaded costs stay separate from Amazon-reported costs. COGS are managed by the user via form in the Sellers & Vendors page. Every 5 days DataDoe checks sellers with at least one COGS row and emails organization owners when SKUs sold in the last 30 days have no COGS. To list SKUs sold in the last 30 days without COGS, use GET /api/v1/cogs/missing or the MCP tool cogs_missing_list.

sources.description: Successful Amazon Catalog Items observations per child ASIN and marketplace for items the Organization tracks. A later successful response is retained even when unchanged; a retry keeps the original observation_id and checked_at without adding a duplicate. History starts after the Organization enables it and tracks the item. A newly associated item receives its next successful observation, without older shared-cache history. The source stays off until a staged Connector rollout enables it. History follows the existing catalog refresh. DataDoe can request an item again one day after its last cache update. The catalog worker runs every 15 minutes in each region and stops at its time limit, so a tracked item can go more than one day without a new observation. A history delivery backlog does not stop current catalog refreshes. Failed, throttled, empty and hard-failed attempts and items Amazon omits create no history observation. Missing days and source values remain unknown: a missing item or rank does not mean deletion or a zero rank. Observations are per item, not an atomic snapshot of the whole catalog. Changes occurred between observations; checked_at is not the exact time Amazon edited the item. Use amazon_products_by_child_asin and amazon_products_raw for current-state joins to sales, inventory and profit. They keep one latest row per ASIN and marketplace and provide the cached onboarding baseline. Legacy rows can have null checked_at and observation_id; overwritten payloads are not recovered or assigned invented times. When Amazon omits an item, its current row is created or cleared without a new checked_at and without a history observation. Filter history by child_asin, marketplace_id and a date range; date and snapshot_date are the UTC date of checked_at. For rank trends, order by checked_at and observation_id and compare category names and raw category identifiers, which can change. To compare observations, join on child_asin and marketplace_id and filter the two observation_id values; an absent observation produces no comparison. For the last observed state at a chosen time, filter checked_at <= the chosen timestamp, then use QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY child_asin, marketplace_id ORDER BY checked_at DESC, observation_id DESC) = 1. This returns only items observed by that time and does not fill gaps with current content.

columns.description: Coupon start in UTC. Use this column for date filtering; the table has no date column.

columns.name: end_date_time
columns.description: Coupon end in UTC.

columns.name: is_once_per_customer
columns.description: Whether a vendor coupon can be redeemed once per customer account. Empty on seller coupons.

columns.name: customer_segment
columns.description: Customers who can clip the coupon. Examples: All (Default), Amazon Prime, Amazon Student.

columns.name: clips
columns.description: Times customers applied the coupon on the product page. Coupon-level value repeated on every ASIN row of the coupon. Aggregate by coupon_id before summing.

columns.name: redemptions
columns.description: Times the coupon was used for a purchase, including returned and cancelled orders. Coupon-level value repeated on every ASIN row of the coupon. Aggregate by coupon_id before summing.

columns.name: budget
columns.description: Budget allocated to the coupon for discounts and clip or redemption fees. Present for seller coupons and for vendor campaigns with PER_INDIVIDUAL_COUPON. Empty when the vendor campaign uses SHARED_BUDGET.

columns.name: total_discount
columns.description: Amount customers saved with the coupon, including returned and cancelled orders. Coupon-level value repeated on every ASIN row of the coupon. Aggregate by coupon_id before summing.

columns.name: budget_spent
columns.description: Amount spent on the coupon, including clip fees and redemption fees, and including returned and cancelled orders. Coupon-level value repeated on every ASIN row of the coupon. Aggregate by coupon_id before summing.

columns.name: budget_remaining
columns.description: budget minus budget_spent. Empty when the vendor campaign uses SHARED_BUDGET.

columns.name: budget_percentage_used
columns.description: Percent of allocated budget spent, on a 0-100 scale. A value of 0.4 means 0.4 percent. For a shared vendor budget this is versus the campaign budget.

columns.name: sales
columns.description: Seller coupon revenue after the discount, including returned and cancelled orders. Empty on vendor coupons. Coupon-level value repeated on every ASIN row of the coupon. Aggregate by coupon_id before summing.

columns.name: merchant_id
columns.description: Seller merchant customer id. Empty on vendor coupons.

columns.name: promotions_api_mapping_id
columns.description: Identifier for joining this coupon to amazon_promotions.

columns.name: asin
columns.description: Child ASIN included in the coupon. One row per ASIN.

columns.name: discount_type
columns.description: PERCENT_OFF_LIST_PRICE or AMOUNT_OFF_LIST_PRICE for this ASIN.

columns.name: discount_amount
columns.description: Customer discount on this ASIN. A percent of list price when discount_type is PERCENT_OFF_LIST_PRICE (10 means 10 percent). A currency amount when discount_type is AMOUNT_OFF_LIST_PRICE.

sources.description: Seller and vendor coupon performance, one row per coupon and ASIN. Includes clips, redemptions, budget, and the ASIN discount. Campaign and coupon totals repeat on every ASIN row. Vendor rows carry campaign, vendor code, and Subscribe and Save; sales is seller coupon revenue. Filter on start_date_time. Join amazon_promotions on promotions_api_mapping_id.

sources.description: Invoice-level lines of Vendor Central payments. One row per line of a payment: invoice payments, deductions, vendor returns, and advertising. A deduction shows only through description, invoice_type, and a negative amount; there is no reason code, dispute, or purchase order field. One invoice can be paid across several payments, so amount_paid is the part paid by this payment. Join amazon_remittances on unique_payment_id and amazon_invoices on invoice_number. date is the UTC day of the parent payment date.

sources.description: DataDoe invoice product costs and reconciled settlement margins. One row per scoped invoice. date remains the invoice issue date; final_settlement_date attributes the complete settlement history once. Partial payments show cash immediately but have no final margin. Costs use the invoice issue date. Unmatched identities, history or tax leave settlement margin unavailable. Nonzero deductions linked to the same invoice number or purchase order also withhold that invoice margin. Other payment-level deductions remain visible without blocking individual invoice margins. Backdated edits and reopening recompute this current view. Not complete net profit.

sources.description: Vendor codes assigned by Amazon, uploaded per ASIN or SKU. Each row has exactly one of child_asin or sku set. ASIN-based sales tables prefer an explicit ASIN upload and can resolve SKU uploads through an unambiguous Vendor Listings mapping. Every 5 days DataDoe checks vendors with at least one vendor code row and emails organization owners when ASINs sold in the last 30 days have no vendor code. To list ASINs sold in the last 30 days without a vendor code, use GET /api/v1/vendor-codes/missing or the MCP tool vendor_codes_missing_list.

sources.description: Weekly forward customer-demand forecast per child ASIN from the Amazon Vendor Forecasting report. Each request returns only the latest forecast. DataDoe stores each weekly fetch as a snapshot keyed by date (forecast generation date). Amazon forecasts week 0 through week 47 from that date, so each snapshot has 48 forward weeks (start_forecasting_date and end_forecasting_date). The same week can appear on later snapshots. Filter to MAX(date) per child_asin and week for the current forecast. Rows are not additive across date snapshots.

The views overlap and must not be added together. customer_country_code is the shipment destination. marketplace_country_code identifies the connection marketplace, not the customer or warehouse country. sources.description: Daily sales, traffic and inventory metrics per child ASIN. Columns prefixed manufacturing_retail_ are Amazon manufacturing-view metrics for all ASINs the vendor manufactures. Columns prefixed sourcing_retail_ are Amazon sourcing-view metrics for ASINs this vendor sourced directly to Amazon (distributor view). DataDoe fetches both views and joins them onto one ASIN-day; the prefixes are overlapping views, not two independent facts and not additive — never sum them or revenue and units double-count. Shipped units/revenue often match because Amazon returns the same shippedOrders in both views; matching is expected, not a copied row. Ordered units/revenue exist only under manufacturing. Contra-COGS is typically populated only under sourcing. Use manufacturing_retail_ for glance views, customer-ordered units/revenue (retail demand, not purchase orders), and net PPM. Use sourcing_retail_ for purchase-order fill metrics (vendor_confirmation_rate, received_fill_rate) and contra-COGS. Amazon-to-vendor purchase-order quantity is amazon_vendor_purchase_orders.ordered_quantity. Either prefix alone is valid for shipped revenue/COGS — pick one view per analysis, not both. Shipped COGS, shipped revenue, contra-COGS, and Net PPM measure Amazon retail economics, not the vendor's own product margin. net_pure_product_margin is a convenience alias of manufacturing_retail_net_ppm (both read manufacturing net_ppm); do not cross-check them as independent series. On-hand, aged, unhealthy, in-transit, and open purchase-order units are end-of-period snapshots and are not additive across days. For a monthly balance, use the latest available date in the month, then aggregate across ASINs if needed. Columns prefixed manufacturing_business_ and sourcing_business_ are Amazon Business selling-program sales on the same ASIN-day. They come from GET_VENDOR_SALES_REPORT, not Retail Data Kiosk. Manufacturing and sourcing Business views overlap and are not additive. Do not subtract Business from Retail. Shipped COGS is the price Amazon paid the vendor. Shipped revenue is Amazon's customer revenue. Ordered revenue and units are customer demand and exist only on the manufacturing Business view. Customer returns are units customers returned. The Business report has no traffic, inventory, Net PPM, or vendor co-op. Dates stay on Amazon's Pacific reporting date.

Rates and averages, including net PPM, vendor confirmation rate, received fill rate, sell-through, Ultra Fast Track, sourceable replenishment out-of-stock, and lost Featured Offer, are Amazon figures for this period. Do not average or sum ASIN or daily rows to recreate them. Shipped COGS, shipped revenue, contra-COGS, and Net PPM measure Amazon retail economics, not the vendor's own product margin. Inventory and open purchase-order units are end-of-period snapshots and are not additive across periods. Columns prefixed manufacturing_retail_ are Amazon manufacturing-view metrics for all ASINs the vendor manufactures. Columns prefixed sourcing_retail_ are Amazon sourcing-view metrics for ASINs this vendor sourced directly to Amazon (distributor view). DataDoe fetches both views and joins them onto one ASIN-day; the prefixes are overlapping views, not two independent facts and not additive — never sum them or revenue and units double-count. Shipped units/revenue often match because Amazon returns the same shippedOrders in both views; matching is expected, not a copied row. Ordered units/revenue exist only under manufacturing. Contra-COGS is typically populated only under sourcing. Use manufacturing_retail_ for glance views, customer-ordered units/revenue (retail demand, not purchase orders), and net PPM. columns.name: manufacturing_retail_unsellable_in_transit_inventory

sources.description: Weekly catalog totals for one Vendor connection and marketplace. Weeks start on Sunday and end on Saturday. Amazon returns one total for the catalog. It is not the sum of ASIN rows. Rates and averages, including net PPM, vendor confirmation rate, received fill rate, sell-through, Ultra Fast Track, sourceable replenishment out-of-stock, and lost Featured Offer, are Amazon figures for this period. Do not average or sum ASIN or daily rows to recreate them. Shipped COGS, shipped revenue, contra-COGS, and Net PPM measure Amazon retail economics, not the vendor's own product margin. Inventory and open purchase-order units are end-of-period snapshots and are not additive across periods. Columns prefixed manufacturing_retail_ are Amazon manufacturing-view metrics for all ASINs the vendor manufactures. Columns prefixed sourcing_retail_ are Amazon sourcing-view metrics for ASINs this vendor sourced directly to Amazon (distributor view). DataDoe fetches both views and joins them onto one ASIN-day; the prefixes are overlapping views, not two independent facts and not additive — never sum them or revenue and units double-count. Shipped units/revenue often match because Amazon returns the same shippedOrders in both views; matching is expected, not a copied row. Ordered units/revenue exist only under manufacturing. Contra-COGS is typically populated only under sourcing. Use manufacturing_retail_ for glance views, customer-ordered units/revenue (retail demand, not purchase orders), and net PPM. Use sourcing_retail_ for purchase-order fill metrics (vendor_confirmation_rate, received_fill_rate) and contra-COGS. Amazon-to-vendor purchase-order quantity is amazon_vendor_purchase_orders.ordered_quantity. Either prefix alone is valid for shipped revenue/COGS — pick one view per analysis, not both. Amazon returns inventory for the current week and the previous seven weeks. Older weekly inventory stays empty. Sales and traffic history is about two years.

sources.description: Monthly sales, traffic, and inventory per child ASIN. Months start on day 1. Rates and averages, including net PPM, vendor confirmation rate, received fill rate, sell-through, Ultra Fast Track, sourceable replenishment out-of-stock, and lost Featured Offer, are Amazon figures for this period. Do not average or sum ASIN or daily rows to recreate them. Shipped COGS, shipped revenue, contra-COGS, and Net PPM measure Amazon retail economics, not the vendor's own product margin. Inventory and open purchase-order units are end-of-period snapshots and are not additive across periods. Columns prefixed manufacturing_retail_ are Amazon manufacturing-view metrics for all ASINs the vendor manufactures. Columns prefixed sourcing_retail_ are Amazon sourcing-view metrics for ASINs this vendor sourced directly to Amazon (distributor view). DataDoe fetches both views and joins them onto one ASIN-day; the prefixes are overlapping views, not two independent facts and not additive — never sum them or revenue and units double-count. Shipped units/revenue often match because Amazon returns the same shippedOrders in both views; matching is expected, not a copied row. Ordered units/revenue exist only under manufacturing. Contra-COGS is typically populated only under sourcing. Use manufacturing_retail_ for glance views, customer-ordered units/revenue (retail demand, not purchase orders), and net PPM. Use sourcing_retail_ for purchase-order fill metrics (vendor_confirmation_rate, received_fill_rate) and contra-COGS. Amazon-to-vendor purchase-order quantity is amazon_vendor_purchase_orders.ordered_quantity. Either prefix alone is valid for shipped revenue/COGS — pick one view per analysis, not both. Amazon returns inventory for the current month and the previous 23 months. Older monthly inventory stays empty. Sales and traffic history is about two years. For a stock balance, use the latest month, then add ASINs if you need a catalog figure. Prefer the monthly catalog total when Amazon has already calculated it.

sources.name: Sales, Traffic & Inventory by Month

sources.description: Monthly catalog totals for one Vendor connection and marketplace. Months start on day 1. Amazon returns one total for the catalog. It is not the sum of ASIN rows. Rates and averages, including net PPM, vendor confirmation rate, received fill rate, sell-through, Ultra Fast Track, sourceable replenishment out-of-stock, and lost Featured Offer, are Amazon figures for this period. Do not average or sum ASIN or daily rows to recreate them. Shipped COGS, shipped revenue, contra-COGS, and Net PPM measure Amazon retail economics, not the vendor's own product margin. Inventory and open purchase-order units are end-of-period snapshots and are not additive across periods. Columns prefixed manufacturing_retail_ are Amazon manufacturing-view metrics for all ASINs the vendor manufactures. Columns prefixed sourcing_retail_ are Amazon sourcing-view metrics for ASINs this vendor sourced directly to Amazon (distributor view). DataDoe fetches both views and joins them onto one ASIN-day; the prefixes are overlapping views, not two independent facts and not additive — never sum them or revenue and units double-count. Shipped units/revenue often match because Amazon returns the same shippedOrders in both views; matching is expected, not a copied row. Ordered units/revenue exist only under manufacturing. Contra-COGS is typically populated only under sourcing. Use manufacturing_retail_ for glance views, customer-ordered units/revenue (retail demand, not purchase orders), and net PPM. Use sourcing_retail_ for purchase-order fill metrics (vendor_confirmation_rate, received_fill_rate) and contra-COGS. Amazon-to-vendor purchase-order quantity is amazon_vendor_purchase_orders.ordered_quantity. Either prefix alone is valid for shipped revenue/COGS — pick one view per analysis, not both. Amazon returns inventory for the current month and the previous 23 months. Older monthly inventory stays empty. Sales and traffic history is about two years.

sources.description: Lookup of DataDoe Amazon accounts for Seller Central, Vendor Central, Amazon Ads, and Amazon DSP. One row per connection, plus one row per Amazon DSP advertiser mapped to a seller or vendor on a shared agency Ads account. A DSP-only agency seat is not its own seller. seller_or_vendor_id equals connection_context_id and is not unique: one context can have a Seller Central row, an Amazon Ads row, and one row per DSP advertiser. columns.description: Portfolio ID for SPONSORED_PRODUCTS campaigns. Null for SPONSORED_DISPLAY and SPONSORED_BRANDS.

columns.description: Portfolio name for SPONSORED_PRODUCTS campaigns. Null for SPONSORED_DISPLAY and SPONSORED_BRANDS.

columns.name: ad_sales
columns.description: Products: same-SKU click sales (7d). Display: promoted-product click sales (14d). Brands: estimated share of campaign sales (14d), including brand halo. Use ad_sales_same_sku for the product-only scope. The advertised-product total, including other products and Display view-through sales, is ad_attributed_sales.

columns.name: ad_orders
columns.description: Products: same-SKU click orders (7d). Display: promoted-product click orders (14d). Brands: estimated share of campaign orders (14d), including brand halo. Use ad_orders_same_sku for the product-only scope.

columns.name: ad_sales_same_sku
columns.description: Attributed sales of the advertised SKU only (14d for SPONSORED_BRANDS and SPONSORED_DISPLAY, 7d for SPONSORED_PRODUCTS). Excludes brand-halo purchases of other SKUs. Not total ad sales; campaign totals are amazon_ads_performance_by_campaign_by_date.ad_sales. Null for Sponsored Brands.

columns.name: ad_clicks
columns.description: Clicks after Amazon removed invalid traffic. Gross clicks, including invalid traffic, are ad_gross_click_throughs. Null for Sponsored Brands.

columns.name: ad_impressions
columns.description: Times the ad was displayed after Amazon removed invalid traffic. Gross impressions, including invalid traffic, are ad_gross_impressions. Null for Sponsored Brands.

columns.name: ad_spend
columns.description: Reported Products and Display spend, or estimated Brands spend allocated to this ASIN and SKU. Sponsored Brands spend uses eligible ad-creative ASINs, with same-day ad cost rescaled to campaign cost. Remaining spend uses campaign purchased-product shares. Without purchased-product data, it uses Seller Central sales, orders and sessions, or an even split among known campaign ASINs. Sales and orders allocate campaign totals by purchased-product shares, with the same fallback signals. ASIN spend and sales are split across available SKUs by same-day order-sales shares; orders use order-count shares. A zero total uses an even split for that measure. With no SKU rows, sku is null. Campaigns without any ASIN signal remain account-only. Attribution windows do not apply to spend.

columns.name: ad_units_sold_same_sku
columns.description: Products: same-SKU click-attributed units (7d), excluding brand halo. Display: total click-attributed units (14d), which can include purchases of other products despite the column name. Null for Brands.

columns.name: ad_orders_same_sku
columns.description: Attributed orders of the advertised SKU only (14d for SPONSORED_BRANDS and SPONSORED_DISPLAY, 7d for SPONSORED_PRODUCTS). Excludes brand-halo orders of other SKUs. Null for Sponsored Brands.

columns.name: ad_attributed_sales
columns.description: Sales attributed to this ad, including other products. Sponsored Products uses a 7-day click window. This is the Sales figure on Amazon's advertised-product report. Sponsored Display includes sales from clicks and views, so view-through sales are included. The value is null for Sponsored Brands. For Sponsored Products, ad_sales is only the same-SKU part. Do not add ad_sales to this column.

columns.name: ad_attributed_orders
columns.description: Orders attributed to this ad, including other products. Sponsored Products uses a 7-day click window. Sponsored Display includes orders from clicks and views, so view-through orders are included. The value is null for Sponsored Brands. For Sponsored Products, ad_orders is only the same-SKU part. Do not add ad_orders to this column.

columns.name: ad_attributed_units_sold
columns.description: Units attributed to this ad, including other products. Sponsored Products uses a 7-day click window. Sponsored Display includes units from clicks and views, so view-through units are included. The value is null for Sponsored Brands.

columns.name: ad_campaign_budget_amount
columns.description: Campaign budget repeated on every row of the campaign. Do not sum it across ASINs, keywords, placements, or dates. ad_campaign_budget_type is DAILY_BUDGET or LIFETIME_BUDGET. Available for Sponsored Products. Null for Sponsored Display and Sponsored Brands.

sources.description: Ads performance by product, ad or campaign, and date for Sponsored Products, Sponsored Display, and Sponsored Brands. Multiple rows can exist for the same ASIN, SKU and date. ad_sales and ad_orders are same-SKU click sales for Sponsored Products and promoted-product click sales for Sponsored Display. ad_attributed_sales, ad_attributed_orders and ad_attributed_units_sold are the advertised-product report totals, including other products. Sponsored Display totals include view-through sales. Display ad_units_sold_same_sku includes all click-attributed units. Brands ad_sales and ad_orders are estimated shares of campaign totals, including brand halo. Brands same-SKU columns, attributed columns, clicks and impressions are null. Sponsored Brands spend uses eligible ad-creative ASINs, with same-day ad cost rescaled to campaign cost. Remaining spend uses campaign purchased-product shares. Without purchased-product data, it uses Seller Central sales, orders and sessions, or an even split among known campaign ASINs. Sales and orders allocate campaign totals by purchased-product shares, with the same fallback signals. ASIN spend and sales are split across available SKUs by same-day order-sales shares; orders use order-count shares. A zero total uses an even split for that measure. With no SKU rows, sku is null. Campaigns without any ASIN signal remain account-only. Estimates can lag the campaign report and are revised as inputs arrive. Prefer amazon_ads_performance_by_campaign_by_date for total campaign data. Sponsored Television and Amazon DSP are not included here.

dataAvailability.description: Daily fetch starts at 2am and rereads 21 days. Intraday fetches start at 8am, 1pm and 4pm and reread 5 days. Times use the marketplace time zone. Data is available after processing and can change in later reports.

Amazon reports no cost, impressions, or clicks at ASIN level; spend is in amazon_ads_dsp_performance_by_creative_by_date. sources.description: Amazon DSP inventory performance per advertiser, date, order, line item, site or app, supply source, deal, and currency. Amazon DSP only (DataDoe DSP slot of a seller or vendor), refreshed once a day, not intraday. Rows map to a seller or vendor through seller_or_vendor_id, which is null when the DSP advertiser is not mapped. DSP order = campaign and line item = ad group in the new Amazon DSP naming. The table stays off until the Organization turns it on. Once enabled, it uses the DSP advertiser ID configured on each Seller or Vendor. No separate advertiser or connection selection is needed. Each Amazon request is one day and one DSP order. The first fetch covers 56 days, a daily refresh covers 14 days, and a monthly refresh covers 56 days so Amazon can restate conversions. ad_currency is budgetCurrency. Do not add monetary values across currencies. Site, supply source, and deal stay null when Amazon omits them, and deal can be Unallocated. There is no app or site classification. ad_sales, ad_orders, ad_detail_page_views, and ad_add_to_cart come from metric.sales, metric.purchases, metric.detailPageViews, and metric.addToCart and are the intended promoted-plus-halo totals. Columns ending in _promoted come from the matching Promoted fields. Amazon DSP 14-day attribution after an ad view or click.

columns.description: Shopper window used to compute the metrics: 1w (one week), 1m (one month), or 1cm (one calendar month). Not an ads attribution window.

columns.name: awareness_index
columns.description: Awareness index. Percentile of this brand versus peers in the category. Not a 0–1 rate and not a shopper count. Brand Metrics covers all on-Amazon shopping, not only ad-attributed events.

columns.name: consideration_index
columns.description: Consideration index. Percentile of this brand versus peers in the category. Not a 0–1 rate and not a shopper count. Brand Metrics covers all on-Amazon shopping, not only ad-attributed events.

columns.name: sales_index
columns.description: Sales index. Percentile of this brand versus peers in the category. Not a 0–1 rate and not a shopper count. Brand Metrics covers all on-Amazon shopping, not only ad-attributed events.

columns.name: add_to_carts
columns.description: Shoppers who added this brand to cart in the category and lookback. A shopper count, not ad-attributed add-to-carts.

columns.name: add_to_carts_return_on_engagement
columns.description: Return on engagement: average sales over the following year from shoppers who were in this funnel state 12 months ago. A currency amount, not a rate, and not ad-attributed sales.

columns.name: brand_customers
columns.description: Shoppers who purchased and account for the bottom 90% of this brand’s sales in the category and lookback. High-value customers are the top 10%.

columns.name: brand_customers_return_on_engagement
columns.description: Return on engagement: average sales over the following year from shoppers who were in this funnel state 12 months ago. A currency amount, not a rate, and not ad-attributed sales.

columns.name: branded_searches_and_detail_page_views
columns.description: Shoppers who searched the brand and viewed a detail page in the category and lookback. A shopper count, not ad impressions.

columns.name: branded_searches_and_detail_page_views_return_on_engagement
columns.description: Return on engagement: average sales over the following year from shoppers who were in this funnel state 12 months ago. A currency amount, not a rate, and not ad-attributed sales.

columns.name: branded_searches_only
columns.description: Shoppers who searched the brand and did not engage further or purchase in the category and lookback.

columns.name: customer_conversion_rate
columns.description: Share of shoppers who moved from considering this brand to purchasing in the lookback. A percentage, not an order count.

columns.name: engaged_shopper_rate_lower_bound
columns.description: Lower bound of engaged-shopper rate: unique shoppers this brand engaged or who purchased, divided by unique shoppers with at least one detail-page view in the category. A percentage bound, not a shopper count.

columns.name: engaged_shopper_rate_upper_bound
columns.description: Upper bound of the same engaged-shopper rate. Read with engaged_shopper_rate_lower_bound.

columns.name: high_value_customers
columns.description: Top 10% of shoppers by sales contribution for this brand in the category and lookback. brand_customers is the other 90%.

columns.name: high_value_customers_return_on_engagement
columns.description: Return on engagement: average sales over the following year from shoppers who were in this funnel state 12 months ago. A currency amount, not a rate, and not ad-attributed sales.

columns.name: new_to_brand_customer_rate
columns.description: Share of customers who had not purchased this brand in the prior 12 months and did purchase in the lookback. A percentage, not a customer count.

columns.name: new_to_brand_sns_customers_rate
columns.description: Share of new-to-brand customers who are Subscribe & Save customers. A percentage, not a customer count.

columns.name: total_sns_customers
columns.description: Subscribe & Save customers of this brand in the category and lookback. A customer count.

columns.name: viewed_detail_page_only
columns.description: Shoppers who viewed a detail page and did not engage further or purchase in the category and lookback.

columns.name: viewed_detail_page_only_return_on_engagement
columns.description: Return on engagement: average sales over the following year from shoppers who were in this funnel state 12 months ago. A currency amount, not a rate, and not ad-attributed sales.

sources.description: Amazon Ads Brand Metrics: brand-level awareness, consideration, and sales indices plus the shopping funnel (branded searches, detail-page views, add-to-carts, brand customers, high-value customers, return on engagement), by brand, category node, computation date, and lookback. Indices are percentiles versus peers, not 0–1 rates. This is all on-Amazon shopping, not ad-attributed performance. Sparse — most metric columns are NULL for a given row. Columns ending in _category_median are the peer median. Columns ending in _category_top_performers or _category_performers are the average of the 95th–99th percentile of peers. Columns ending in _return_on_engagement, or containing _roe_, are return on engagement (currency), not rates.

sources.description: Target performance by target and date. Sponsored Products includes keywords and product targets. Sponsored Brands includes product targets and broad, phrase and exact keywords. Keyword rows appear after the keyword report is collected. The first keyword load covers the latest 30 completed days. Keyword refreshes run every two days and replace the latest 14 completed days. Keyword rows have no monthly refresh. The table refresh periods apply to the other campaign types. The keyword report does not cover every Sponsored Brands campaign. A global Ads account keeps keyword rows for the connection marketplace only. Campaign status and budget on keyword rows come from the Sponsored Brands campaign report for the same connection, date and campaign. Sponsored Display includes product, category, and remarketing targets such as views and purchases. Display ad_match_type is blank, Amazon audience segments are not included, and Display spend and impressions can be lower than the campaign table for the same campaign. Sponsored Television is included. ad_keyword is the target. The shopper query is amazon_ads_search_terms_by_campaign_by_date.ad_search_term. Do not sum this table into campaign totals.

sources.description: Daily account-wide search impression share and rank for Sponsored Products and Sponsored Brands. One row is one Ads connection, advertiser account, ad product, search term, date, and occurrence. A global advertiser account covers several marketplaces, and Amazon reports a search term once per marketplace without saying which one: a term with search_term_occurrences above 1 ran in several marketplaces of the account. Every Ads connection of the same advertiser account holds a copy of the account's rows; to count an account once across all sellers and vendors of the Organization, filter is_account_primary_copy = TRUE. Do not use that filter for one seller or vendor or a subset of them: the marked copy can belong to a connection outside the selection. marketplace_id is the marketplace of the connection that fetched the account's report, not of the row. impression_share is Amazon's percentage from 0% to 100%, not a ratio from 0 to 1. impression_share_rank is a positive whole number when Amazon sends it. Do not add shares or average ranks across dates, accounts, or search terms. This is not ad_top_of_search_impression_share on a keyword, and it is not amazon_ads_recommendation_snapshots. Sponsored Display, Sponsored Television, and Full-Funnel are not included. A product with no rows does not have 0% share. The first fetch covers the latest 30 completed days in the advertiser account's Ads reporting time zone. A refresh every two days covers the latest 21 completed days and replaces those days, including search terms that are no longer in the file and dates with no rows. Today is not included. The marketplace time zone is used only when the reporting time zone is not stored.

columns.description: Sponsored Products attributed sales of the advertised SKU within seven days. Null for other ad types.

columns.name: ad_sales_other_sku
columns.description: Sponsored Products attributed sales of SKUs other than the advertised SKU within seven days.

columns.name: ad_units_same_sku
columns.description: Sponsored Products units of the advertised SKU attributed within seven days.

columns.name: ad_units_other_sku
columns.description: Sponsored Products units of other SKUs attributed within seven days.

columns.name: purchased_product_other_sku_sales
columns.description: Target-level sum of seven-day other-SKU sales from the purchased-products report. Null for search terms and unsupported ad types.
columns.definition: sum(raw Sponsored Products purchased-products salesOtherSku7d) by target and date

columns.name: purchased_product_sales_delta
columns.description: Target other-SKU sales minus purchased-product other-SKU sales. The difference remains visible even when it is within the accepted tolerance.

columns.name: estimated_cogs_same_sku
columns.description: Estimated COGS for same-SKU sales. Target rows use ad-group advertised-product unit mix; search-term rows inherit the parent target cost per same-SKU sale.
columns.definition: same-SKU units times promoted-product unit COGS mix, or search-term same-SKU sales times parent same-SKU COGS divided by parent same-SKU sales

columns.name: estimated_cogs_other_sku
columns.description: Estimated COGS for other-SKU sales. Target rows use purchased ASIN units and scale costs to reported other-SKU sales within the reconciliation tolerance. Search-term rows inherit the parent target cost per other-SKU sale.
columns.definition: target: sum(purchased ASIN units * estimated unit COGS) * ad_sales_other_sku / purchased_product_other_sku_sales; search term: other-SKU sales * parent other-SKU COGS / parent other-SKU sales

columns.name: estimated_variable_fees_same_sku
columns.description: Estimated same-SKU order fees from the advertised-product mix and preceding 90 days of SKU ORDER settlements. Uses the account profit fee definition; excludes refunds.
columns.definition: same-SKU units times historical per-unit fee mix, or search-term same-SKU sales times parent fees divided by parent same-SKU sales

columns.name: estimated_variable_fees_other_sku
columns.description: Estimated other-SKU order fees from purchased ASINs and preceding 90 days of SKU ORDER settlements, scaled within the reconciliation tolerance. Excludes refunds.
columns.definition: target: sum(purchased ASIN units * historical unit fees) * ad_sales_other_sku / purchased_product_other_sku_sales; search term: other-SKU sales * parent other-SKU fees / parent other-SKU sales

columns.name: estimated_cogs
columns.description: Sum of estimated same- and other-SKU COGS. Null when either sold component cannot be costed.
columns.definition: estimated_cogs_same_sku + estimated_cogs_other_sku when all sold components are costed

columns.name: cogs_present
columns.description: True when positive Sponsored Products sales match the same- and other-SKU split within 0.01 and every positive component has a COGS estimate. False if the split or an estimate is missing or the split does not match; null when reported sales are not positive or this campaign type does not support cost estimates.

columns.name: estimated_variable_fees
columns.description: Estimated order fees, net of order credits, using the same fee families as account profit: referral, closing, digital services, fulfillment (including handling, pick and pack, transportation and order-level return charges), technology and seller-funded promotions. Excludes refunds, advertising, seller-retained tax and posted-date fees such as storage, subscription, inbound and disposal. Null without sufficient history.
columns.definition: estimated_variable_fees_same_sku + estimated_variable_fees_other_sku; per-SKU unit fee = orderDateTotalFeesSum(ORDER settlements in preceding 90 days) / sum(order-SKU quantities counted once across split settlement rows), scoped to seller connection, marketplace and currency

columns.name: estimated_contribution_before_ads
columns.description: Attributed sales less estimated COGS and variable fees, before ad spend. Null for incomplete costs.

columns.name: estimated_profit_after_ads
columns.description: Attributed contribution less reported spend, excluding refunds. Recent rows are provisional until attribution matures and remain in daily profit summaries. This estimate must not be added to account P&L.

columns.name: estimated_break_even_acos
columns.description: Maximum ad spend divided by attributed sales that leaves estimated contribution after ads at zero. Ratio, not percent; null with no sales or incomplete costs.

columns.name: acos
columns.description: Reported ad spend divided by attributed sales. Ratio, not percent; null with no sales.

columns.name: costed_sales
columns.description: Attributed sales from rows with a non-null profit estimate, including provisional rows.

columns.name: unsupported_sales
columns.description: Attributed sales from ad types without product attribution for estimating profit.

columns.name: missing_cost_sales
columns.description: Sponsored Products sales on rows without a profit estimate because costs, parent target data or reconciliation are incomplete. Includes the whole row, even if one sales component has costs.
columns.definition: ad_campaign_type === 'SPONSORED_PRODUCTS' && ad_sales > 0 && estimated_profit_after_ads is null ? ad_sales : 0

columns.name: cost_coverage_rate
columns.description: Share of same- and other-SKU sales components with COGS and fee estimates. May include a component of a row whose total profit is null. Ratio, not percent.
columns.definition: sum(same- and other-SKU sales components with COGS and fee estimates) / ad_sales

columns.name: cost_assignment_method
columns.description: Method used to assign product costs. Target costs use promoted-product and purchased-ASIN mix; search terms inherit parent target mix.

columns.name: profit_status
columns.description: PENDING_ATTRIBUTION while a known attribution window is still open. Otherwise ESTIMATED, SPEND_ONLY, ATTRIBUTION_UNAVAILABLE, SELLER_CENTRAL_CONNECTION_UNAVAILABLE, MISSING_PRODUCT_COST_OR_FEE, PARENT_TARGET_UNAVAILABLE or PRODUCT_ATTRIBUTION_UNAVAILABLE. Pending rows can have provisional profit values.
columns.definition: pending attribution takes precedence; then campaign type, reported sales availability, parent availability, Seller Central connection and missing costs determine status

columns.name: profitability_flag
columns.description: Business reading of this daily estimate: PROFITABLE (at or above break-even), BELOW_BREAK_EVEN, NO_SALES_MATURE or INSUFFICIENT_DATA. Pending attribution is insufficient for a final decision. A single no-sales day is not a recommendation to pause a target.
columns.definition: immature: INSUFFICIENT_DATA; mature with zero sales and positive spend: NO_SALES_MATURE; null profit: INSUFFICIENT_DATA; positive sales and profit >= 0: PROFITABLE; negative profit: BELOW_BREAK_EVEN; otherwise INSUFFICIENT_DATA

columns.name: excludes_refunds
columns.description: Always true. Estimates exclude refund revenue reversals, refund fees and returned-product cost recovery. Break-even ACoS is before the cost of refunds.

columns.name: purchased_asin_cost_method
columns.description: How purchased-ASIN unit costs are assigned: SINGLE_SKU, SHARED_SKU_COST, RECENT_ORDER_UNIT_MIX or MIXED across purchased ASINs. Search terms inherit this from the parent. Null without a purchased mix.
columns.definition: Within the seller connection, marketplace and currency, use a common unit cost when all known SKUs agree; otherwise weight available SKU costs by order quantities from the preceding 90 days. Require costs for every SKU with positive order weight; no supported weights means null costs. The SKU set comes from effective COGS and recent ORDER settlements.

columns.name: is_attribution_mature
columns.description: Whether the full report attribution window has elapsed since the click date in the marketplace timezone.

columns.name: mature_spend_without_sales
columns.description: Reported spend with zero attributed sales after the attribution window has elapsed. Null otherwise.

sources.description: One row per target present in the collected reports and click date. Includes Sponsored Products keywords and product or automatic targets, Sponsored Brands product targets and broad, phrase and exact keywords after the keyword report is collected, and reported Display and Television targets. This is partial report coverage, not all account advertising. Spend and attributed sales are reported metrics. Sponsored Products COGS and fees are estimates from uploaded COGS, purchased ASINs, advertised-product mix and preceding 90 days of Seller Central ORDER settlements. For purchased ASINs with several SKUs, use shared unit costs or recent order quantities as weights within the seller connection. Accept purchased sales and units within max(2% of the target value, 0.01), and scale costs by target other-SKU sales / purchased sales. Other campaign types keep reported metrics but have null profit estimates. Refund costs are excluded and recent profit is provisional. This is an ad decision view; its profit does not add to amazon_profit_by_date.profit.

sources.description: Entity settings from complete published Universal Ads exports, including unchanged later observations. Each snapshot_id is one family/profile export, not a simultaneous account snapshot. Actual observation dates and gaps are authoritative. Portfolio names are null in campaign history; seller and account labels are current context. Absence from a later file does not imply deletion. Changes are known only between observations.  History follows existing collection, normally every 48 hours, with large targets on the weekly schedule. Source caps and failed or incomplete exports leave gaps. No complete daily coverage is guaranteed. Inspect checked_at and snapshot manifests for actual observations. Actions provide live entity state.

columns.description: Amazon Ads campaign id. Use it with the Ads connection, not on its own.

columns.name: currency
columns.description: Currency of the measures on this row. Do not combine different currencies.

columns.name: time_window_starts_at
columns.description: UTC start of the Amazon activity window. This is not the time the event was received. Events with no start stay on AMS Traffic and AMS Conversion and are not given an hour.

columns.name: time_window_ends_at
columns.description: UTC end of the activity window, 1 hour after time_window_starts_at.

columns.name: reporting_timezone
columns.description: IANA timezone of the Amazon Ads profile, such as Europe/London. Null when that timezone is not verified. There is no UTC fallback.

columns.name: reporting_timezone_source
columns.description: ADS_PROFILE when reporting_timezone is verified. UNKNOWN when it is not.

columns.name: date
columns.description: Calendar date of the activity window in reporting_timezone. Filter on this date, then group by weekday and local_hour. Null when the timezone is unknown. A retention period uses this date, so those rows are removed when retention is set.

columns.name: date_utc
columns.description: UTC calendar date of the activity window. This is a diagnostic, not the local date.

columns.name: local_hour
columns.description: Hour of the activity window in reporting_timezone, from 0 to 23. Null when the timezone is unknown. Repeated local hours during daylight saving stay on separate UTC windows.

columns.name: weekday
columns.description: Local weekday of date. Monday is 1 and Sunday is 7. Null when the timezone is unknown.

columns.name: weekday_name
columns.description: English name of weekday. Use weekday for grouping.

columns.name: utc_offset_minutes
columns.description: Minutes between the local activity time and UTC, including the daylight-saving offset. Null when the timezone is unknown.

columns.name: default_click_attribution_window_days

columns.name: traffic_source_rows
columns.description: Count of canonical AMS Traffic events in this row, after repeated deliveries of the same idempotency id are collapsed. 0 when only conversion data is present. This does not prove every hour was collected.

columns.name: conversion_source_rows
columns.description: Count of canonical AMS Conversion events in this row. 0 when only traffic data is present. This is not the conversion count.

columns.description: True when traffic_source_rows is greater than zero.

columns.name: conversion_data_present
columns.description: True when conversion_source_rows is greater than zero.

columns.description: Earliest received time among the traffic events in this row. Null when traffic is absent.

columns.name: traffic_last_received_at
columns.description: Latest received time among the traffic events in this row. Null when traffic is absent.

columns.name: conversion_first_received_at
columns.description: Earliest received time among the conversion events in this row. Null when conversion is absent.

columns.name: conversion_last_received_at

columns.name: source_last_updated_at
columns.description: Latest source dt_updated across the traffic and conversion events in this row.

columns.name: source_presence
columns.description: BOTH, TRAFFIC_ONLY, or CONVERSION_ONLY. This shows which side contributed. It does not mean collection is complete.

columns.name: has_negative_aggregates
columns.description: True when any summed traffic or conversion measure is below zero. Negative corrections stay in the measure.

columns.name: dt_created
columns.description: Earliest source dt_created among the events in this row. Not the time this view was built.

columns.name: dt_updated
columns.description: Same timestamp as source_last_updated_at. Not the current time.

sources.description: Advertising performance for each campaign and each Amazon activity hour. Filter on the local date, then group by weekday and local hour and recompute ratios from the summed measures. Hours use the advertiser's Amazon Ads profile timezone, including daylight saving. If that timezone is unknown, the local date, hour, and weekday are null. A null measure is unavailable, not zero. A missing traffic or conversion side stays null. Turning this table on does not mean the stream is subscribed, receiving, or complete for every past hour. This is not the shopper's purchase hour, and it is not hourly profit, fees, or total advertising cost of sales.
sources.prerequisites: Requires AMS Traffic and AMS Conversion. Turning this table on can turn those tables on and starts collection for every Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands, and Sponsored Display dataset they use. This view does not store a second billed copy of those rows. Rows with row billing on a required table still count toward usage.

A file with other column names leaves the mapped columns empty. These rows do not identify a vendor remittance. The invoice id can match an Ads invoice.

sources.description: Products you can advertise in Amazon Ads, for sellers, vendors, and books, with Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands, and Sponsored Display eligibility. One row per Organization, DataDoe Store, Ads connection, marketplace, ASIN, and SKU. A missing SKU is null. Eligibility belongs to that Ads account, not to the ASIN in every account. A missing program status is unknown, not a denial. Amazon DSP is not included. Each Ads connection refreshes every three days, with at most 10,000 products per program. Account permissions and Amazon API availability apply. observed_at_utc is the time of the latest product observation. Existing exports stay on amazon_ads_book_catalog until you select this table. Migration examples: https://app.datadoe.com/hub/docs/datadoe-data/ads-product-catalog.

sources.description: Estimated KDP author earnings and profit after ads for Sponsored Products ads, ad groups and campaigns by date, using 14-day attribution. Only Ads connections with KDP royalty parameters for the AMAZON channel. Units are costed per purchased edition with the parameters effective on the date; KENP royalties are Amazon estimates. Estimates are provisional until is_attribution_mature_14d. Do not sum AD, AD_GROUP and CAMPAIGN rows together; filter one entity_type.

columns.name: connection_context_id
columns.description: DataDoe connection context id, or the connection id when no context is set. Same value as seller_or_vendor_id. Not a unique row key when one context has several connections or DSP advertisers.

columns.name: connection_context_name
columns.description: Context display name. Same value as seller_or_vendor_name. Falls back to the connection name, then the connection id. DSP rows use the mapped context name.

columns.name: seller_or_vendor_id
columns.description: Same value as connection_context_id. DataDoe account id used by MCP and API calls (sellers_and_vendors_list, exports). Not unique on this table: repeated for each connection and each DSP advertiser in the context. Fact tables copy this value into their seller_or_vendor_id.

columns.name: seller_or_vendor_name
columns.description: Same value as connection_context_name. DataDoe display name for the seller or vendor context.

columns.name: ads_dsp_connection_id
columns.description: DataDoe Amazon Ads connection id of the account Amazon DSP is run from. One agency connection can be shared by several sellers or vendors. Null on non-DSP rows. Join DSP facts on organization_id, store_id, ads_dsp_connection_id, and dsp_advertiser_id.

columns.name: dsp_advertiser_id
columns.description: Amazon DSP advertiser identifier mapped to this seller or vendor. One advertiser maps to one context. If an advertiser is reassigned, only the latest mapping is kept. Null on non-DSP rows.

columns.name: selling_partner_id
columns.description: Amazon selling partner id from the connection (connection_seller_id). Same value as marketplace_seller_id. This is the Amazon id, not seller_or_vendor_id. Null on DSP advertiser rows and when the connection has no seller id.

columns.name: marketplace_seller_id
columns.description: Same value as selling_partner_id: Amazon connection_seller_id. Null on DSP advertiser rows and when the connection has no seller id.

columns.name: amazon_ads_profile_id
columns.description: Amazon Ads profile id. Set on Amazon Ads connections and on DSP advertiser rows. Null on Seller Central and Vendor Central rows.

columns.name: marketplace_id
columns.description: Amazon provided ID that represents a specific country where the Seller or Vendor operates.

columns.name: ads_account_type
columns.description: Amazon Ads profile account type: seller / vendor / agency. Null until DataDoe captured the profile. Null on Seller Central, Vendor Central and DSP advertiser rows.

columns.name: ads_account_subtype
columns.description: Amazon Ads special account subtype, such as KDP_AUTHOR or AMAZON_ATTRIBUTION. Null for regular accounts and until DataDoe captured the profile. Null on Seller Central, Vendor Central and DSP advertiser rows.

columns.name: is_kdp_author
columns.description: True for a Kindle Direct Publishing author account (ads_account_subtype KDP_AUTHOR), false for other captured profiles. Null until DataDoe captured the profile. Null on Seller Central, Vendor Central and DSP advertiser rows.

columns.name: ads_profile_currency_code
columns.description: Currency of the Amazon Ads profile. Null until DataDoe captured the profile. Null on Seller Central, Vendor Central and DSP advertiser rows.

columns.name: ads_profile_timezone
columns.description: IANA timezone of the Amazon Ads profile. Null until DataDoe captured the profile. Null on Seller Central, Vendor Central and DSP advertiser rows.

columns.name: amazon_ads_reporting_timezone
columns.description: IANA timezone from the Amazon Ads profile, such as Europe/London. Null when it is not verified. Seller Central and Vendor Central rows are null. DSP rows use the agency Ads connection timezone, not a DSP advertiser timezone. There is no country or UTC fallback.

columns.name: amazon_ads_reporting_timezone_source
columns.description: ADS_PROFILE when amazon_ads_reporting_timezone is verified. UNKNOWN when it is not.

columns.name: ads_billing_permission_missing_at
columns.description: When the last Ads Billing check for this connection was denied. Null when the last check succeeded, the connection is not Amazon Ads, or billing has not been checked. DSP advertiser rows are null.

sources.description: Lookup of DataDoe Amazon accounts for Seller Central, Vendor Central, Amazon Ads, and Amazon DSP. One row per connection, plus one row per Amazon DSP advertiser mapped to a seller or vendor on a shared agency Ads account. A DSP-only agency seat is not its own seller. seller_or_vendor_id equals connection_context_id and is not unique: one context can have a Seller Central row, an Amazon Ads row, and one row per DSP advertiser. Join Seller Central and Vendor Central facts on sp_connection_id or vendor_connection_id. Attribute DSP facts on organization_id, store_id, ads_dsp_connection_id, and dsp_advertiser_id.
